one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: Virginia SCC local public hearings Oct 7 (Newport News) and Oct 9 (Fairfax), which will generate critical headlines but rarely move the merits; a possible SCC ruling on the AG's motion to treat the Sep 14 supplement as an amendment (granting it pushes the deadline from Jan 11 to ~March 2027, a mild negative for timing); Q3 2026 results, date not confirmed by NEE IR (TipRanks says Oct 22; Q3 2025 was Oct 28), both inside the window, where a small beat and a reaffirmed 8%+ plan are likely but priced; and the Oct 28 FOMC, where swaps-implied hike odds fell to ~36% after the cool Sep 30 PCE (that relief is already in the $75.91 close). Possible Uri headlines (the trial date is unset) are small in dollars. The stock sits near its 52-week low after a 23% drawdown, so I allow a slight mean-reversion tilt (median ~$76.1) and use ~6.3% monthly sigma (21%/3.5 plus a bit for clustered events), with a slightly fatter left tail.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E on NTM EPS at Sep-2027 (~$4.58 = 0.25 x 2027E $4.33 + 0.75 x 2028E $4.67) x 17.5x = $80.2 (60%) and dividend yield (2027 run-rate $2.64 / 3.35% = $78.8, 40%) = ~$79.5. The multiple is held slightly below today's ~17.9x NTM because of the 5%+ 10-yr, the Dominion overhang (including a $4.83B NEE-paid regulatory break fee) and the Oklahoma Uri liability; the expected Uri cost (~$0.1-0.3/share) is inside rounding.

inputs_detail.value: 8%+ CAGR through 2032 standalone; 2026 $3.92-4.02, high end targeted; reaffirmed Jul 24 and Sep 14

inputs_detail.derivation: $3.71 x 1.08^2 = $4.33 (2027E), x 1.08^3 = $4.67 (2028E); NTM = 0.25 x 4.33 + 0.75 x 4.67 = $4.58. The round-1 trim for financing costs is dropped: management reaffirmed 8%+ twice and I found no evidence of a cut.

Today's NTM multiple is ~17.9x ($75.9 / ~$4.25 NTM). I hold 17.5x rather than 17x: I no longer assume further de-rating from rates alone (10-yr 5.24% on Sep 28, easing after PCE), but I keep a ~0.4x discount for skeptic-lane overhangs the market will still be carrying at Sep-2027: the unresolved Dominion approvals with a $4.83B NEE-paid break fee if they fail, the Uri damages trial, and equity funding of heavy capex.
Today's yield is ~3.28% ($2.49 / $75.9). I use a slightly higher 3.35% because the 10-yr is near its highest since 2007 and deal/litigation overhangs persist; a 3.28% yield would give $80.5.

bear.story: 10-yr pushes to 5.5-6%, utilities de-rate further; the Virginia SCC restarts the clock and imposes burdensome conditions or signals rejection, so the market prices the $4.83B (~$2.30/share) NEE-paid regulatory break fee; Uri damages come in at the high end (~$0.5/share on ~$1B); multiple compresses to ~13x on ~$4.40 NTM EPS.

base.story: EPS compounds ~8% (2026 ~$4.01, 2027 ~$4.33); yields stabilize around 4.75-5.25%; SCC approves with conditions in Q1 2027 and the deal moves toward close in H2 2027; Uri damages are a few hundred million; the stock trades ~17.5-18x NTM EPS of $4.58.

bull.story: Yields fall back toward 4.3%, the deal is approved cleanly, and large-load/data-center contracting supports 9%+ combined growth; multiple back to ~21.5x NTM $4.58.

thesis_break_reason: $60 is ~13.1x NTM EPS of ~$4.58 and a ~4.4% yield on the $2.64 2027 dividend run-rate, below the 2023 rate-shock trough. At that level the market would be pricing a fundamental break rather than rates: a cut to the 8%+ EPS or 6% dividend plan, forced equity or an S&P/Moody's outlook change (S&P 17% FFO/debt, Moody's 16% CFO pre-WC/debt), a Virginia burdensome condition or rejection that puts the $4.83B break fee in play, or a multi-billion Uri judgment.

reasoning: Skeptic lane, round 2. I accepted the supervisor's corrections: NTM EPS at the horizon is a 2027/2028 blend (~$4.58), not full-year 2028; the dividend run-rate is $2.49 ($0.6232/qtr), giving $2.64 for 2027; I dropped my unsupported financing-cost trim to EPS; there are Virginia local hearings on Oct 7/9 inside the 1-month window; October hike odds fell to ~36% after the Sep 30 PCE; and the Q3 date is unconfirmed. New bear-side facts I added: NEE pays Dominion a $4.83B (~$2.30/share) regulatory termination fee if the deal fails on regulatory grounds (DEFM14A). This is in my bear case, although it could only be paid after the horizon. I tried to size the Uri exposure: coverage of the Sep 29 ruling gives no NEM figure, and the AG speaks of 'billions' across all sellers statewide. But Oklahoma Watch reports Macquarie sold $154M of gas to Oklahoma utilities and the AG hoped for >$100M recovery in the related cases. So NEM's plausible damages are ~$0.2-1B (~$0.1-0.5/share, ~0.1-0.6% of market cap): a headline risk, not a thesis changer, and an appeal is likely. On the multiple: supervisor noted my 17x sat below today's ~17.9x NTM. I move to 17.5x and a 3.35% target yield, keeping a small skeptic discount for the deal, the break fee, Uri and equity funding, but not assuming further rate-driven de-rating. Fair value rises from $78 to ~$79.5 (P/E $80.2 at 60%, dividend $78.8 at 40%), still slightly below the group. Scenarios are $58 / $81 / $99 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$79.8). The ladder is roughly lognormal around a ~$79.5 median, with ~25% vol below and ~23% above (slightly fat left tail for the rate, deal and credit events), giving P(>=76) ~0.57. The consensus PT of ~$98-100 is treated as lagging evidence, not the answer. Research was limited to ~5 extra queries; the NonDoc article was blocked (403).
